summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Linkage is the co-inheritance of genes located on the same chromosome due to physical proximity. Morgan's Drosophila Cross I (yellow body y and white eye w) showed tight linkage with 98.7% parental and 1.3% recombinant types. Cross II (white eye w and miniature wing m) showed loose linkage with 62.8% parental and 37.2% recombinant types. Alfred Sturtevant developed genetic mapping: 1% Recombination Frequency = 1 Map Unit = 1 centimorgan (cM).

LINKAGE vs RECOMBINATION

         ▼                                                       ▼
   TIGHT LINKAGE                                           LOOSE LINKAGE
   Genes positioned close together.                        Genes positioned far apart.
   ├── High Parental Phenotypes (~99%)                     ├── Higher Recombinants (up to 50%)
   └── Low Recombinants (Morgan's Cross I: 1.3%)           └── Morgan's Cross II: 37.2%
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 7.1 Morgan's Dihybrid Linkage Crosses in *Drosophila*

```
                     MORGAN'S LINKAGE CROSS COMPARISON
                     
   CROSS I (Yellow body y, White eye w):
   ├── Parental Types  = 98.7%
   └── Recombinants    = 1.3%  ──► Tightly linked on X-chromosome.
   
   CROSS II (White eye w, Miniature wing m):
   ├── Parental Types  = 62.8%
   └── Recombinants    = 37.2% ──► Loosely linked on X-chromosome.
```

### 7.2 Genetic Mapping by Alfred Sturtevant
- Sturtevant recognized that **recombination frequency (RF) is directly proportional to the physical distance** separating two gene loci on a chromosome.

$$\text{Recombination Frequency (RF)} = \frac{\text{Number of Recombinant Progeny}}{\text{Total Number of Progeny}} \times 100$$

$$\mathbf{1\%\text{ Recombination}} = \mathbf{1\text{ Map Unit (m.u.)}} = \mathbf{1\text{ centimorgan (cM)}}$$

```
                            GENE MAPPING EXAMPLE
                            
   Given Recombination Frequencies:
   ├── Gene A - Gene B = 10% (10 cM)
   ├── Gene B - Gene C = 15% (15 cM)
   └── Gene A - Gene C = 5%  (5 cM)
   
   Map Order: A ── (5 cM) ── C ─────── (15 cM) ─────── B
              └──────────────── (10 cM) ──────────────┘
```

- **Maximum Recombination Threshold**: The maximum observable recombination frequency between two linked genes on a single chromosome is **$50\%$**, above which the cross behaves indistinguishably from unlinked genes undergoing independent assortment.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Coupling (Cis) vs Repulsion (Trans) Phases
conceptBreakdown.title: Coupling (Cis) vs Repulsion (Trans) Phases
conceptBreakdown.content: Bateson & Punnett observed that dominant alleles entering from the same parent tend to be inherited together (Coupling / Cis: AB/ab), whereas dominant alleles from opposite parents tend to separate (Repulsion / Trans: Ab/aB).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Interference and Coincidence in Three-Point Crosses
conceptBreakdown.title: Interference and Coincidence in Three-Point Crosses
conceptBreakdown.content: The Coefficient of Coincidence (C) is the ratio of Observed Double Crossovers to Expected Double Crossovers; positive interference ($I = 1 - C$) indicates that a crossover in one region suppresses nearby crossovers.
